verification_note: Every url re-opened. The Secretary of State's 2022 general, 2024 general and 2024 primary precinct workbooks were downloaded and summed by race: Racki (Cascade County Attorney, DEM, 18,551, sole candidate) and Metz (Richland Treasurer/Assessor, REP, 3,386, sole candidate) confirmed; Nikolakakos won HD 26 in 2022 (REP, 1,206 to 890) and HD 22 in 2024 (REP, 2,017 to 1,225); Smith lost HD 39 in 2024 (DEM, 1,624 to 3,151); Anderson lost HD 67 in 2024 (DEM, 2,170 to 3,757); Roland lost the 2024 HD 62 Democratic primary (448, third of the field on that ballot); Dugan placed first of six for Whitefish Local Government Study Commissioner in 2024; Chiko Olson's Lewis and Clark Precinct 3 lies in House District 79 (the same workbook's HD 79 rows), giving the second anchor. Corrections: Nikolakakos's HD 26 office now rests on the official 2022 results instead of an uncited and self-contradicting Wikipedia infobox, with years matching the Legislature's record (HD 22 term from November 5, 2024); Vannatta's appointment wording follows the county page; McLaughlin's website note follows what the site shows (its /about page answers 404).
note: The session's shared web search allowance ran out after five searches in this part, so most findings come from pages opened directly: the Montana Free Press 2026 legislative guide (to find campaign sites, each then opened and checked), the Secretary of State's official precinct-by-precinct results workbooks for the 2022 and 2024 primary and general elections (searched for every name in this part; party labels as printed), the Legislature's own legislator record (bearbeta.legmt.gov, the service behind legislators.legmt.gov), and county websites. Not found or not recorded: campaign sites for candidates the guide lists without one (none were guessed); Jeffrey Lundberg is listed on Sanders County's Justice Court page as a clerk and restitution officer, a staff job, not an office, so nothing is recorded; Rio Roland's 2024 run for the Bozeman study commission is nonpartisan and the city's page does not list him as a member, so it is left out; George Nikolakakos's Wikipedia birth date carries no citation, so it is left out. Precinct committee seats were treated as party posts, not offices; the one kept (Chiko Olson) is recorded only as a run on a party's primary ballot. Endorsements and slate cards for this part are already in ballot/lean/mt_endorsements.json. Blank means not found, not that nothing exists.
